title: Local Minimax Limit for Adaptive Neyman Allocation with Rare Events

gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is the unrestricted minimax crossover and controlled-Poisson decision limit; logarithmic raw-IPW tracking behavior already appears in [ClipSMT](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.14341v1), and the variance identities supply supporting infrastructure. Its scope remains a one-parameter rare-treatment experiment with known local scale, known control raw second moment, and a fixed IPW estimator family. The coefficient 1/4 characterizes the limiting value after the rare-event limit, while compact-horizon convergence does not establish a joint endpoint-uniform finite-experiment expansion; the framing preserves this distinction without a stale sharpness claim. Enumeration of all policy trees establishes computability but supplies neither a scalable crossover policy nor numerical evaluation of the continuum value, and the reported numerical audits lack accompanying reproducible code in the delivered package. These scope and implementation limitations constrain the projected paper score, although the proved decision characterization clears the field floor. proof_attempt_summary: Derived the rare-treatment all-policy regret frontier and strengthened it to a controlled-Poisson local minimax decision limit, with certificates and endpoint constants. D0.5 mathematics passed with no findings and all seven citations verified, but the cold package assessment was subfield (ceiling 6.7 below 7.4), not salvageable within scope. No conjecture was refuted; no F stages or Lean modules were produced, and four editorial/ballast findings remain disclosed.
tldr: The rare-event Neyman design problem has an exact local decision limit: with \(x=n\rho^{3/2}\), the normalized value \(\rho R^*(n,\rho)\) converges to the unrestricted controlled-Poisson value \(V(x)\), locally uniformly on compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\). Computable finite saddle policies attain this limit, and their dual priors give matching approximating certificates. The posterior dynamic program characterizes the Bayes value. Its endpoints are \(V(x)=C_{\rm blind}x+o(x)\) as \(x\downarrow0\) and \(V(x)=\tfrac14\log x+o(\log x)\) as \(x\to\infty\). The finite-horizon frontier is \(R^*(n,\rho)\asymp\rho^{-1}\log(1+n\rho^{3/2})\). These results hold for all binary-treatment, signed-control pair laws with the prescribed treatment marginal, allowing the full control-mean interval \([-1,1]\). They include the originally requested interval \([-1/2,1/2]\) as an immediate corollary. Regret divided by \(n^2\) is exactly oracle excess MSE within the specified IPW family.
gap: Published raw-IPW tracking results give algorithmic logarithmic upper bounds; the target gap is a uniform local all-policy regret frontier and its exact decision refinement. Adaptive Horvitz--Thompson unbiasedness and raw-second-moment variance accounting are known supporting infrastructure. A bounded-control Poisson approximation does not settle an adaptive minimax limit.
fill: An audited policy and a full-state Bayesian converse target the finite-sample order theorem. The exposure posterior and finite saddle program specify the exact decision question, including exploration compactification, least-favorable priors and the sharp large-horizon coefficient. A common-seed magnitude coupling supplies a self-contained raw-regret identity. Known variance accounting gives the causal precision interpretation.
